dek: A reviewed agent harness uses registry conformance and runtime tests to check generated AI instrumentation.

stories.title: OpenTelemetry checks agent-written instrumentation against a shared registry
stories.summary: An agent harness builds instrumentation, checks its emitted telemetry with Weaver, and returns violations for repair. Engineers still review the plan and framework mappings.
body: OpenTelemetry defines shared ways to record application activity. An engineering report from Alibaba Cloud describes a harness that uses agents to build instrumentation for generative AI frameworks. Instrumentation records operations as spans, the individual steps within a trace. Choosing where those steps begin and end, and mapping their data consistently, requires framework knowledge.

First, research agents inspect public hooks and callbacks. A reviewed execution plan fixes the instrumentation points before coding begins. Agents then implement that plan using shared utilities and run code review and unit tests. Next, framework examples run in a Kubernetes test cluster, and Weaver compares their emitted telemetry with a registry of shared definitions. A violation returns the work for repair; passing checks lead to a sustained runtime test for memory leaks and regressions.

The authors replaced an earlier model-based conformance reviewer because it sometimes approved invalid output. Registry checks still cannot establish that framework operations were mapped correctly, so human review remains necessary. Attribute-coverage measurements also run separately without blocking builds. The authors report human-reviewed plugins in LoongSuite and ongoing work to bring them into OpenTelemetry’s Python GenAI project. Instrumentation cannot recover execution details a framework does not expose.
stories.takeaway: Framework maintainers can separate registry conformance from lifecycle coverage and runtime testing. Keep human review of instrumentation points even when generated code passes automated checks.

image_provenance.prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: standalone newspaper editorial infographic PNG. Explain the OpenTelemetry instrumentation validation loop, based on https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2026/agent-harness-genai-instrumentation/. Warm ivory newsprint, dark ink, muted teal accents, fine editorial linework, generous spacing, landscape 3:2. Title verbatim: "Check the telemetry, then test the runtime". Four connected boxes left to right with exact labels: "Reviewed plan", "Generated instrumentation", "Weaver registry check", "Runtime soak test". Below Weaver draw a return arrow to Generated instrumentation labelled "Violation: repair and repeat". Below final box small note: "Human review still checks framework mappings". Source facts: engineers review the plan; agents implement instrumentation; Weaver compares emitted telemetry to a registry; violations return to coding; passing checks lead to soak tests for memory leaks and regressions. Depict one simple conceptual workflow, no performance claims, no logos, no screenshots, no footer or watermark. Large clear type readable at article width.

stories.score_reason: Concrete instrumentation workflow with executable conformance checks, explicit failure feedback and documented human-review limits.
